ITEM 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations 
 the Company designs, develops, markets and sells athletic footwear, apparel, equipment, accessories and services worldwide. We are the largest seller of athletic footwear and apparel in the world. We sell our products to retail accounts, through the Company-owned in-line and factory retail stores and the Company-owned internet websites (which we refer to as our “Direct to Consumer” or "DTC" operations), and through a mix of independent distributors, licensees and sales representatives in virtually all countries around the world. Our goal is to deliver value to our shareholders by building a profitable global portfolio of branded footwear, apparel, equipment and accessories businesses. Our strategy is to achieve long-term revenue growth by creating innovative, “must have” products, building deep personal consumer connections with our brands and delivering compelling consumer experiences at retail and online. 
 In addition to achieving long-term, sustainable revenue growth, we continue to strive to deliver shareholder value by driving operational excellence in several key areas:

(1) 
 During fiscal 2020, we divested of Umbro and Cole Haan, allowing us to focus our resources on driving growth in the the Company, Product B, Product A and Hurley brands. As of May 31, 2020, we had substantially completed all transition services related to the sale of both businesses. The results of the divestitures are presented as discontinued operations. Please refer to Note 15 — Discontinued Operations in the accompanying Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements for more detail.

(5) 
 References to the Company Brand wholesale equivalent revenues are intended to provide context as to the total size of our the Company Brand market footprint if we had no Direct to Consumer operations. the Company Brand wholesale equivalent revenues consist of (1) sales to external wholesale customers and (2) internal sales from our wholesale operations to our Direct to Consumer operations which are charged at prices that are comparable to prices charged to external wholesale customers.

On a wholesale equivalent basis and excluding the effects of changes in currency exchange rates, fiscal 2021 the Company Brand Men's revenues increased 9% mainly as a result of strong growth in our Basketball, Football (Soccer), Running and Sportswear categories. Women's revenues increased 12% in large part due to increases in our Running, Sportswear and Women's Training categories. The 16% increase in the Young Athletes' business was driven by increases in the Basketball and Football (Soccer) categories in part due to our expanded footwear and apparel offerings for this age group. 
 Futures Orders 
 Futures orders for the Company Brand footwear and apparel scheduled for delivery from June through November 2022 were 2% higher than the orders reported for the comparable prior year period. The U.S. Dollar futures order amount is calculated based upon our internal forecast of the currency exchange rates under which our revenues will be translated during this period. Excluding the impact of currency changes, futures orders increased 13%, with unit orders and average selling price per unit contributing approximately 8 and 5 percentage points of growth, respectively.

The reported futures orders growth is not necessarily indicative of our expectation of revenue growth during this period. This is due to year-over-year changes in shipment timing, changes in the mix of orders between futures and at-once orders and because the fulfillment of certain orders may fall outside of the schedule noted above. In addition, exchange rate fluctuations as well as differing levels of order cancellations, discounts and returns can cause differences in the comparisons between futures orders and actual revenues. Moreover, a portion of our revenue is not derived from futures orders, including sales of at-once and closeout the Company Brand footwear and apparel, sales of the Company Brand equipment, sales from our DTC operations and sales from Product A, the Company Golf and Hurley.

Fiscal 2022 Compared to Fiscal 2021 
 On a currency-neutral basis, fiscal 2022 revenues for Emerging Markets increased 8%, driven by growth in 7 of 9 territories. Growth was led by one of our largest territories, SOCO (which includes Argentina, Uruguay and Chile), which grew 28%, and our Pacific territory (which includes Australia and New Zealand), which grew 26%. Revenues in our Mexico and Brazil territories decreased 21% and 3%, respectively. The decrease in Mexico was attributable to efforts to liquidate excess inventory in the marketplace largely resulting from an inconsistent flow of product to customers following distribution center transition issues in fiscal 2021, while the decrease in Brazil was primarily due to challenging macroeconomic conditions and comparison to strong sales related to the World Cup in fiscal 2021. On a category basis, revenues were higher in most key categories, led by Sportswear, Running and Basketball, partially offset by a decline in Football (Soccer). DTC revenues increased 51% compared to fiscal 2021, driven by strong comparable store sales growth of 26%, the addition of new stores and online sales growth.
In both purchasing scenarios, a weaker U.S. Dollar decreases the inventory cost incurred by the Company whereas a stronger U.S. Dollar increases its cost.

For the currency within the factory currency exposure indices that is the local or functional currency of the factory, the currency rate fluctuation affecting the product cost is recorded within Inventories and is recognized in Cost of sales when the related product is sold to a third-party. All currencies within the indices, excluding the U.S. Dollar and the local or functional currency of the factory, are recognized as embedded derivative contracts and are recorded at fair value through Other (income) expense, net . rebuttals.innocent_explanation: The 10.1% revenue growth (E25) is consistent with management's cited drivers of category strength, 51% DTC growth (E38), and emerging markets growth (E38). The DSO improvement from 45 to 40 days (E25) aligns with a shift toward DTC sales, which typically collect cash faster than wholesale. The quarterly revenue deceleration (E27-E30) reflects tougher year-over-year comparisons and possible shipment timing variations noted in E37. However, the pack lacks segment revenue data to quantify the exact contribution of each driver.

The 2.2% decline in year-end receivables (E7, E19) alongside 10.1% revenue growth (E25) mechanically improves DSO, and the quarterly DSO trend shows consistent improvement each quarter (E27-E30: 42→41, 45→43, 44→40, 42→39). This pattern is consistent with a shift toward DTC sales (which management reports grew 51% in E38) and/or tighter credit management, and is not indicative of revenue overstatement. The shipment timing caveat in E37 and currency remeasurement in E41 may also contribute.

The 55.8% surge in operating cash flow (E6, E18, E26) is driven by 21.5% net income growth (E5, E17), a $104.1M reduction in receivables (E7, E19), and a $1.79B increase in current liabilities (E11, E23) which includes payables and accrued expenses. The payable to Sojitz America on 60-day terms (E42) and letters of credit for inventory (E43) suggest extended payment terms may have contributed. The current assets increase of $3.12B (E8, E20) partly reflects higher cash and inventory, but the net working capital change favors cash flow. The Beneish M-score of -2.80 (E31) indicates no earnings manipulation signal.

rebuttals.innocent_explanation: The reported numbers show revenue growth of 10.1%, receivables decline of 2.2%, DSO improvement of 5 days, and CFO increase of 55.8%. These patterns are consistent with management's stated drivers of Emerging Markets growth and DTC expansion, as DTC sales typically have lower receivables and faster cash conversion. The CFO increase is quantitatively explained by a $794.6M net income increase (E5, E17), a $104M receivables decrease (E7, E19), and a $1.79B increase in current liabilities (E11, E23). The quarterly revenue deceleration from +14.5% in Q1 to +4.8% in Q4 (E27-E30) reflects tougher year-over-year comparisons. However, the pack does not contain segment revenue data to quantify the exact contribution of Emerging Markets and DTC to overall growth.

Mexico's 21% revenue decline is a territory-specific issue within Emerging Markets; the overall Emerging Markets currency-neutral growth of +8% (E38) reflects offsetting strength in other territories (SOCO +28%, Pacific +26%). The pack does not provide Mexico-specific financials, so its isolated impact on consolidated receivables and cash flow cannot be determined, but the aggregate Emerging Markets performance is positive.

Brazil's 3% decline is attributed to macroeconomic headwinds and a tough comparison to World Cup-related sales in FY2021; the overall Emerging Markets growth of +8% currency-neutral (E38) indicates other territories more than offset this decline. The pack lacks Brazil-specific financials to isolate its effect on consolidated metrics.

Management's caution that futures orders are not necessarily indicative of revenue growth due to shipment timing, order mix changes, and fulfillment timing (E37) is a standard disclosure. The quarterly revenue growth deceleration from +14.5% in Q1 to +4.8% in Q4 (E27-E30) and the receivables peak in Q1 followed by decline (E27-E30) are consistent with normal timing variations and do not contradict the disclaimer.

The slight receivables decline of 2.2% and 5-day DSO improvement (E25) could be influenced by currency remeasurement of non-functional currency receivables (E41), but the magnitude of the receivables change (-$104M) is small relative to the balance ($4.7B) and the DSO improvement suggests operational collection improvements are the dominant factor. The pack does not quantify the currency impact.

The 55.8% CFO increase ($2.3B) is quantitatively explained by the $794.6M net income increase (E5, E17), a $104M decrease in receivables (E7, E19), and a $1.79B increase in current liabilities (E11, E23), which together account for the bulk of the CFO surge. The receivables decline contributed modestly; the primary driver was the buildup of current liabilities (payables, accruals) during a period of revenue growth. No explicit management explanation is needed because the numbers themselves provide the reconciliation.

red_team.overall: The investigator's verdict stands for the revenue growth drivers, as the evidence pack lacks segment-level data to verify the size and impact of Emerging Markets and DTC contributions. However, the CFO surge and receivables decline are fully explained by the reported changes in net income, receivables, and current liabilities, contradicting the claim that no explanation exists for these patterns.

red_team.overall: The investigator's verdict that the explanation fits the numbers stands because the reported revenue growth, receivables decline, DSO improvement, and CFO surge are all quantitatively consistent with the disclosed DTC mix shift and category strength. The only unverified finding is the explicit causal link between DTC growth and cash flow acceleration, but the numerical pattern strongly supports it.

rulings.reason: The reported MD&A growth rates for categories (E36) and DTC (E38) align with the observed 10.1% revenue growth, 2.2% receivables decline, 5-day DSO improvement (E25), and 55.8% CFO surge (E26). Quarterly signals (E27-E30) show progressive DSO improvement consistent with a mix shift toward faster-collecting DTC sales.

Quarterly receivables and DSO signals (E27-E30) show no receivables buildup despite revenue growth, supporting management's caution that futures orders (E36) are not indicative of revenue growth due to timing and mix differences.

The 21% Mexico decline and the stated cause (inventory liquidation from distribution center issues) are only reported in MD&A (E38) with no corroborating segment-level financial data in the evidence pack (e.g., Mexico revenue, inventory, or receivables). The overall Emerging Markets growth of 8% is also only from MD&A.

The MD&A excerpts (E32-E43) do not contain an explicit causal explanation linking the receivables decline or CFO surge to DTC growth or other drivers. The consistency of the pattern with DTC growth (E38) is suggestive but not an explicit management explanation.

judge.deciding_evidence: E25 (revenue growth 10.1% with receivables decline 2.2% and DSO improvement 45->40 days) and E27-E30 (quarterly DSO improving each quarter)
evidence_that_would_settle_it: Segment revenue and inventory data for Mexico to verify the 21% decline and inventory liquidation claim
DTC revenue dollar amounts and working capital cash flow breakdown to quantify the impact of DTC shift on CFO and receivables
